053/**
054 *  <p>{@summary This class consists of several utility methods working on
055 *  {@link Object}
056 *  instances, similar to those on
057 *  {@link Arrays}
058 *  or
059 *  {@link Collections}.}</p>
060 *  <p>The class was originally inspired by the class of the same name that
061 *  was finally introduced with the Java&nbsp;7 release; some of its methods
062 *  will delegate to
063 *  {@link java.util.Objects java.util.Objects},
064 *  others will extend the functionality of the methods with the same
065 *  name from {@code java.util.Objects}.</p>
066 *  <p>If a method from {@code java.util.Objects} would throw a
067 *  {@link NullPointerException},
068 *  the method with the same name from this class would throw a
069 *  {@link IllegalArgumentException}
070 *  instead.</p>
071 *
072 *  @author Thomas Thrien - thomas.thrien@tquadrat.org
073 *  @version $Id: Objects.java 1258 2026-06-04 18:33:06Z tquadrat $
074 *  @since 0.0.1
075 *
076 *  @UMLGraph.link
077 */
078@UtilityClass
079@SuppressWarnings( {"ClassWithTooManyMethods", "UseOfObsoleteDateTimeApi", "OverlyComplexClass"} )
080@ClassVersion( sourceVersion = "$Id: Objects.java 1258 2026-06-04 18:33:06Z tquadrat $" )
081@API( status = STABLE, since = "0.0.1" )
082public final class Objects

095    /**
096     *  <p>{@summary Checks if the sub-range from {@code fromIndex} (inclusive)
097     *  to {@code fromIndex + size} (exclusive) is within the bounds of range
098     *  from {@code 0} (inclusive) to {@code length} (exclusive).}</p>
099     *  <p>The sub-range is defined to be out-of-bounds if any of the following
100     *  inequalities is true:</p>
101     *  <ul>
102     *    <li>{@code fromIndex < 0}</li>
103     *    <li>{@code size < 0}</li>
104     *    <li>{@code fromIndex + size > length}, taking into account integer
105     *    overflow</li>
106     *    <li>{@code length < 0}, which is implied from the former
107     *    inequalities</li>
108     *  </ul>
109     *  <p>Calls
110     *  {@link java.util.Objects#checkFromIndexSize(int,int,int) java.util.Objects.checkFromIndexSize(int,int,int)}
111     *  internally.</p>
112     *
113     *  @param  fromIndex   The lower-bound (inclusive) of the sub-interval.
114     *  @param  size    The size of the sub-range.
115     *  @param  length  The upper-bound (exclusive) of the range.
116     *  @return The {@code fromIndex} if the sub-range is within bounds of the
117     *      range.
118     *  @throws IndexOutOfBoundsException   The sub-range is out-of-bounds.
119     *
120     *  @since 0.0.5
121     */
122    @API( status = STABLE, since = "0.0.5" )
123    public static final int checkFromIndexSize( final int fromIndex, final int size, final int length )
124    {
125        final var retValue = java.util.Objects.checkFromIndexSize( fromIndex, size, length );
126
127        //---* Done *----------------------------------------------------------
128        return retValue;
129    }   //  checkFromIndexSize()
130
131    /**
132     *  <p>{@summary Checks if the sub-range from {@code fromIndex} (inclusive)
133     *  to {@code toIndex} (exclusive) is within the bounds of range from
134     *  {@code 0} (inclusive) to {@code length} (exclusive).}</p>
135     *  <p>The sub-range is defined to be out-of-bounds if any of the following
136     *  inequalities is true:</p>
137     *  <ul>
138     *    <li>{@code fromIndex < 0}</li>
139     *    <li>{@code fromIndex > toIndex}</li>
140     *    <li>{@code toIndex > length}</li>
141     *    <li>{@code length < 0}, which is implied from the former
142     *    inequalities</li>
143     *  </ul>
144     *  <p>Calls
145     *  {@link java.util.Objects#checkFromToIndex(int,int,int) java.util.Objects.checkFromToIndex(int,int,int)}
146     *  internally.</p>
147     *
148     *  @param  fromIndex   The lower-bound (inclusive) of the sub-range.
149     *  @param  toIndex The upper-bound (exclusive) of the sub-range.
150     *  @param  length  The upper-bound (exclusive) the range.
151     *  @return The {@code fromIndex} if the sub-range is within bounds of the
152     *      range.
153     *  @throws IndexOutOfBoundsException   The sub-range is out-of-bounds.
154     *
155     *  @since 0.0.5
156     */
157    @API( status = STABLE, since = "0.0.5" )
158    public static final int checkFromToIndex( final int fromIndex, final int toIndex, final int length )
159    {
160        final var retValue = java.util.Objects.checkFromToIndex( fromIndex, toIndex, length );
161
162        //---* Done *----------------------------------------------------------
163        return retValue;
164    }   //  checkFromToIndex()
165
166    /**
167     *  <p>{@summary Checks if the {@code index} is within the bounds of the
168     *  range from {@code 0} (inclusive) to {@code length} (exclusive).}</p>
169     *  <p>The {@code index} is defined to be out-of-bounds if any of the
170     *  following inequalities is true:</p>
171     *  <ul>
172     *    <li>{@code index < 0}</li>
173     *    <li>{@code index >= length}</li>
174     *    <li>{@code length < 0}, which is implied from the former
175     *    inequalities</li>
176     *  </ul>
177     *  <p>Calls
178     *  {@link java.util.Objects#checkIndex(int,int) java.util.Objects.checkIndex(int,int)}
179     *  internally.</p>
180     *
181     *  @param  index   The index.
182     *  @param  length  The upper-bound (exclusive) of the range.
183     *  @return The {@code index} if it is within bounds of the range.
184     *  @throws IndexOutOfBoundsException   The {@code index} is out-of-bounds.
185     *
186     *  @since 0.0.5
187     */
188    @API( status = STABLE, since = "0.0.5" )
189    public static final int checkIndex( final int index, final int length )
190    {
191        final var retValue = java.util.Objects.checkIndex( index, length );
192
193        //---* Done *----------------------------------------------------------
194        return retValue;
195    }   //  checkIndex()

197    /**
198     *  <p>{@summary Throws the exception provided by the given supplier if the
199     *  condition resolves to {@false}.}</p>
200     *  <p>Basically, this method is a replacement for the code sequence
201     *  below:</p>
202     *  <div class="source-container"><pre>…
203     *  if( !&lt;<i>condition</i>&gt; )
204     *  {
205     *      throw new &lt;<i>WhatEver</i>&gt;Exception( &lt;<i>WhatEverMessage</i>&gt; );
206     *  }
207     *  …</pre></div>
208     *  <p>Code using this method may be easier to read than the {@code if}
209     *  statement above:</p>
210     *  <div class="source-container"><pre>…
211     *  checkState( &lt;<i>condition</i>&gt;, () -> new &lt;<i>WhatEver</i>&gt;Exception( &lt;<i>WhatEverMessage</i>&gt; ) );
212     *  …</pre></div>
213     *
214     *  @param  <E> The type of the exception that is thrown in case the
215     *      condition is not met.
216     *  @param  condition   The condition to check.
217     *  @param  exception   The exception to throw.
218     *  @throws E   The condition was not met.
219     */
220    @SuppressWarnings( "CheckedExceptionClass" )
221    public static final <E extends Exception> void checkState( final boolean condition, final Supplier<E> exception ) throws E
222    {
223        requireNonNullArgument( exception, "exception" );
224        if( !condition ) throw exception.get();
225    }   //  checkState()
226
227    /**
228     *  <p>{@summary Returns 0 if the arguments are identical and
229     *  {@code comparator.compare(a, b)} otherwise.}</p>
230     *  <p>Consequently, if both arguments are {@null}, 0 is returned.</p>
231     *  <p>Calls
232     *  {@link java.util.Objects#compare(Object,Object,Comparator) java.util.Objects#compare()}
233     *  internally, but different from that method, this implementation throws
234     *  a
235     *  {@link NullArgumentException}
236     *  in case the {@code comparator} is {@null}.</p>
237     *
238     *  @param  <T> The type of the objects being compared.
239     *  @param  object  An object.
240     *  @param  other   Another object to be compared with the first object.
241     *  @param  comparator  The
242     *      {@link Comparator}
243     *      to compare the first two arguments.
244     *  @return 0 if the arguments are identical and +1, 0, or -1, based on the
245     *      return value of {@code c.compare(a, b)} otherwise.
246     *  @throws NullArgumentException   The {@code comparator} is {@null}.
247     *
248     *  @see Comparable
249     *  @see Comparator
250     *
251     *  @since 0.0.5
252     */
253    @API( status = STABLE, since = "0.0.5" )
254    public static final <T> int compare( final T object, final T other, final Comparator<? super T> comparator ) throws NullArgumentException
255    {
256        final var retValue = object == other ? 0 : signum( java.util.Objects.compare( object, other, requireNonNullArgument( comparator, "comparator" ) ) );
257
258        //---* Done *----------------------------------------------------------
259        return retValue;
260    }   //  compare()
261
262    /**
263     *  <p>{@summary Returns {@true} if the arguments are deeply equal to
264     *  each other and {@false} otherwise.}</p>
265     *  <p>Two {@null} values are deeply equal. If both arguments are
266     *  arrays, the algorithm in
267     *  {@link Arrays#deepEquals(Object[], Object[]) Arrays.deepEquals()}
268     *  is used to determine equality. Otherwise, equality is determined by
269     *  using the
270     *  {@link Object#equals(Object) equals()}
271     *  method of the first argument.</p>
272     *  <p>Calls
273     *  {@link java.util.Objects#deepEquals(Object,Object) java.util.Objects#deepEquals()}
274     *  internally.</p>
275     *
276     *  @param  object  An object.
277     *  @param  other   Another object to be compared with the first object for
278     *      deep equality.
279     *  @return {@true} if the arguments are deeply equal to each other
280     *      and {@false} otherwise.
281     *
282     *  @see    Arrays#deepEquals(Object[],Object[])
283     *  @see    Objects#equals(Object,Object)
284     *
285     *  @since 0.0.5
286     */
287    @SuppressWarnings( "BooleanMethodNameMustStartWithQuestion" )
288    @API( status = STABLE, since = "0.0.5" )
289    public static final boolean deepEquals( final Object object, final Object other ) { return java.util.Objects.deepEquals( object, other ); }
290
291    /**
292     *  <p>{@summary Returns {@true} if the arguments are equal to each
293     *  other and {@false} otherwise.}</p>
294     *  <p> Consequently, if both arguments are {@null}, {@true} is
295     *  returned and if exactly one argument is {@null}, {@false} is
296     *  returned.  Otherwise, equality is determined by using the
297     *  {@link Object#equals(Object) equals()}
298     *  method of the first argument.</p>
299     *  <p>Calls
300     *  {@link java.util.Objects#equals(Object, Object)}
301     *  internally.</p>
302     *
303     *  @param  object  An object.
304     *  @param  other   Another object to be compared with the first one for
305     *      equality.
306     *  @return {@true} if the arguments are equal to each other and
307     *      {@false} otherwise.
308     *
309     *  @see    Object#equals(Object)
310     *
311     *  @since 0.0.5
312     */
313    @API( status = STABLE, since = "0.0.5" )
314    public static final boolean equals( final Object object, final Object other ) { return java.util.Objects.equals( object, other ); }

375    /**
376     *  <p>{@summary Provides a replacement value if the given string value is
377     *  {@null} or empty.}</p>
378     *
379     *  @param  <T> The type of the object to map.
380     *  @param  value   The object to map; can be {@null} (obviously).
381     *  @param  supplier    The supplier for the replacement function.
382     *  @return The provided object if that is not {@null} and not empty, or
383     *      the result from the supplier method. Keep in mind that this result
384     *      can be {@null} or empty!
385     *
386     *  @since 0.25.16
387     */
388    @API( status = STABLE, since = "0.25.16" )
389    public static final <T extends CharSequence> T mapFromEmpty( final T value, final Supplier<? extends T> supplier )
390    {
391        requireNonNullArgument( supplier, "supplier" );
392        final var retValue = isNull( value ) || value.isEmpty()
393            ? supplier.get()
394            : value;
395
396        //---* Done *----------------------------------------------------------
397        return retValue;
398    }   //  mapFromEmpty()
399

484    /**
485     *  <p>{@summary Maps (converts) the given object instance by applying the
486     *  provided mapper if the instance is not {@null}.}</p>
487     *  <p>The mapper function will not be called at all if the given instance
488     *  is {@null}.</p>
489     *
490     *  @param  <T> The type of the object to map.
491     *  @param  <R> The type of the result.
492     *  @param  o   The object to map; can be {@null}.
493     *  @param  mapper  The mapping function.
494     *  @return The result of the mapping, or {@null} if the given object
495     *      instance was already {@null}. Keep in mind that the result of
496     *      the mapping can be {@null}!
497     */
498    public static final <T,R> R mapNonNull( final T o, final Function<T,? extends R> mapper )
499    {
500        @SuppressWarnings( "RedundantExplicitVariableType" )
501        final R retValue = nonNull( o ) ? requireNonNullArgument( mapper, "mapper" ).apply( o ) : null;
502
503        //---* Done *----------------------------------------------------------
504        return retValue;
505    }   //  mapNonNull()
506

509     *  provided mapper if the instance is not {@null} or returns the

512     *  is {@null}.</p>
513     *
514     *  @param  <T> The type of the object to map.
515     *  @param  <R> The type of the result.
516     *  @param  o   The object to map; can be {@null}.
517     *  @param  mapper  The mapping function.
518     *  @param  defaultValue    The default value; can be {@null}.
519     *  @return The result of the mapping, or the default value if the given
520     *      object instance is {@null}. Keep in mind that the result of
521     *      the mapping can be {@null}!
522     */
523    public static final <T,R> R mapNonNull( final T o, final Function<T,? extends R> mapper, final R defaultValue )
524    {
525        @SuppressWarnings( "RedundantExplicitVariableType" )
526        final R retValue = nonNull( o ) ? requireNonNullArgument( mapper, "mapper" ).apply( o ) : defaultValue;
527
528        //---* Done *----------------------------------------------------------
529        return retValue;
530    }   //  mapNonNull()

555    /**
556     *  Applies the given validation on the given value, and if that fails, an
557     *  {@link IllegalArgumentException}
558     *  is thrown.
559     *
560     *  @param  <T> The type of the value to check.
561     *  @param  obj The value to check; can be {@null}.
562     *  @param  validation  The validation
563     *  @return The value if the validation succeeds.
564     *  @throws IllegalArgumentException {@code obj} failed the validation.
565     *
566     *  @since 0.1.0
567     */
568    @SuppressWarnings( "NewExceptionWithoutArguments" )
569    @API( status = STABLE, since = "0.1.0" )

611    /**
612     *  <p>{@summary Applies the given validation on the given value, and if
613     *  that fails, a customized
614     *  {@link IllegalArgumentException}
615     *  is thrown.}</p>
616     *  <p>Unlike the method
617     *  {@link #require(Object,String,Predicate)},
618     *  this method allows to defer the creation of the message until after the
619     *  validation was performed (and failed). While this may confer a
620     *  performance advantage in the success case, some care should be taken
621     *  that the costs for the creation of the message supplier are less than
622     *  the cost of just creating the String message directly.</p>
623     *
624     *  @param  <T> The type of the value to check.
625     *  @param  obj The value to check; can be {@null}.

627     *      in the event that {@code IllegalArgumentException} is thrown. If
628     *      {@null} or if it returns {@null}, no detail message is
629     *      provided to the exception.
630     *  @param  validation  The validation
631     *  @return The value if the validation succeeds.
632     *  @throws NullArgumentException   The validation is {@null}.
633     *  @throws IllegalArgumentException {@code obk} failed the validation.
634     *
635     *  @since 0.1.0
636     */
637    @SuppressWarnings( "NewExceptionWithoutArguments" )
638    @API( status = STABLE, since = "0.1.0" )

642        {
643            final var exception = nonNull( messageSupplier )
644                ? new IllegalArgumentException( messageSupplier.get() )
645                : new IllegalArgumentException();
646            throw exception;
647        }
648
649        //---* Done *----------------------------------------------------------
650        return obj;
651    }   //  require()

903    /**
904     *  <p>{@summary Checks if the given argument {@code arg} is {@null} or
905     *  empty and throws a
906     *  {@link NullArgumentException}
907     *  if it is {@null}, or an
908     *  {@link EmptyArgumentException}
909     *  if it is empty.}</p>
910     *  <p>Strings, arrays, instances of
911     *  {@link java.util.Collection} and
912     *  {@link java.util.Map}
913     *  as well as instances of
914     *  {@link java.lang.StringBuilder},
915     *  {@link java.lang.StringBuffer},
916     *  and
917     *  {@link java.lang.CharSequence}
918     *  will be checked on being empty.</p>
919     *  <p>For an instance of
920     *  {@link java.util.Optional},
921     *  the presence of a value is checked in order to determine whether the
922     *  {@link Optional} is empty or not.</p>
923     *  <p>Because the interface
924     *  {@link java.util.Enumeration}
925     *  does not provide an API for the check on emptiness
926     *  ({@link java.util.Enumeration#hasMoreElements() hasMoreElements()}
927     *  will return {@false} after all elements have been taken from
928     *  the {@code Enumeration} instance), the result for arguments of this
929     *  type has to be taken with caution.</p>
930     *  <p>For instances of
931     *  {@link java.util.stream.Stream},
932     *  this method will only check for {@null} (like
933     *  {@link #requireNonNullArgument(Object,String)}).
934     *  This is because any operation on the stream itself would render it
935     *  unusable for later processing.</p>
936     *  <p>In case the argument is of type
937     *  {@link Optional},
938     *  this method behaves different from
939     *  {@link #requireNotEmptyArgument(Optional,String)};
940     *  this one will return the {@code Optional} instance, while the other
941     *  method will return the contents of the {@code Optional}.</p>
942     *  <p>This method will not work properly for instances of
943     *  {@link java.util.StringJoiner}, because its method
944     *  {@link java.util.StringJoiner#length() length()}
945     *  will not return 0 when a prefix, suffix, or an
946     *  &quot;{@linkplain java.util.StringJoiner#setEmptyValue(CharSequence) empty value}&quot;
947     *  was provided.</p>
948     *
949     *  @param  <T> The type of the argument to check.
950     *  @param  arg The argument to check; may be {@null}.
951     *  @param  name    The name of the argument; this is used for the error
952     *      message.
953     *  @return The argument if it is not {@null} or empty.
954     *  @throws NullArgumentException   {@code arg} is {@null}.
955     *  @throws EmptyArgumentException   {@code arg} is empty.
956     *
957     *  @since 0.0.5
958     */
959    @SuppressWarnings( "OverlyComplexMethod" )
960    @API( status = STABLE, since = "0.0.5" )
961    public static final <T> T requireNotEmptyArgument( final T arg, final String name )
962    {
963        if( isNull( name ) ) throw new NullArgumentException( "name" );
964        if( name.isEmpty() ) throw new EmptyArgumentException( "name" );
965        if( name.isBlank() ) throw new BlankArgumentException( "name" );
966
967        switch( arg )
968        {
969            /*
970             * When using guarding expressions, the code would not get better
971             * to read and to understand, as the positive cases will be handled
972             * all by the default case.
973             */
974            case null -> throw new NullArgumentException( name );
975            case final CharSequence charSequence ->
976            {
977                if( charSequence.isEmpty() ) throw new EmptyArgumentException( name );
978            }
979            case final Collection<?> collection ->
980            {
981                if( collection.isEmpty() ) throw new EmptyArgumentException( name );
982            }
983            case final Map<?,?> map ->
984            {
985                if( map.isEmpty() ) throw new EmptyArgumentException( name );
986            }
987            case final Enumeration<?> enumeration ->
988            {
989                /*
990                 * The funny thing with an Enumeration is that it could have
991                 * been not empty in the beginning, but it may be empty
992                 * (= having no more elements) now.
993                 * The good thing is that Enumeration.hasMoreElements() will
994                 * not change the state of the Enumeration - at least it should
995                 * not do so.
996                 */
997                if( !enumeration.hasMoreElements() ) throw new EmptyArgumentException( name );
998            }
999            case final Optional<?> optional ->
1000            {
1001                /*
1002                 * This is different from the behaviour of
1003                 * requireNotEmptyArgument(Optional,String) as the Optional
1004                 * will be returned here.
1005                 */
1006                if( optional.isEmpty() ) throw new EmptyArgumentException( name );
1007            }
1008            default ->
1009            {
1010                if( arg.getClass().isArray() )
1011                {
1012                    if( Array.getLength( arg ) == 0 ) throw new EmptyArgumentException( name );
1013                }
1014                else
1015                {
1016                    /*
1017                     * Other data types are not further processed; in
1018                     * particular, instances of Stream cannot be checked on
1019                     * being empty. This is because any operation on the Stream
1020                     * itself will change its state and may make the Stream
1021                     * unusable.
1022                     */
1023                }
1024            }
1025        }
1026
1027        //---* Done *----------------------------------------------------------
1028        return arg;
1029    }   //  requireNotEmptyArgument()
1030
1031    /**
1032     *  <p>{@summary Checks if the given argument {@code optional} of type
1033     *  {@link Optional}
1034     *  is {@null} or
1035     *  {@linkplain Optional#empty() empty}
1036     *  and throws a
1037     *  {@link NullArgumentException}
1038     *  if it is {@null}, or a
1039     *  {@link EmptyArgumentException}
1040     *  if it is empty.}</p>
1041     *  <p>Otherwise it returns the value of the {@code Optional}.</p>
1042     *  <p>This is different from the behaviour of
1043     *  {@link #requireNotEmptyArgument(Object,String)}
1044     *  with an instance of {@code Optional} as the argument to test.</p>
1045     *
1046     *  @param  <T> The type of the given {@code Optional} to check.
1047     *  @param  optional    The argument to check; can be {@null}.
1048     *  @param  name    The name of the argument; this is used for the error
1049     *      message.
1050     *  @return The value of the argument if {@code optional} is not
1051     *      {@null}
1052     *      and not
1053     *      {@linkplain Optional#empty() empty}. This could be the empty
1054     *      string!
1055     *  @throws NullArgumentException   {@code optional} is {@null}.
1056     *  @throws EmptyArgumentException   {@code optional} is empty.
1057     *
1058     *  @since 0.0.5
1059     */
1060    @API( status = STABLE, since = "0.0.5" )
1061    public static final <T> T requireNotEmptyArgument( @SuppressWarnings( "OptionalUsedAsFieldOrParameterType" ) final Optional<T> optional, final String name )
1062    {
1063        if( isNull( name ) ) throw new NullArgumentException( "name" );
1064        if( name.isEmpty() ) throw new EmptyArgumentException( "name" );
1065        if( name.isBlank() ) throw new BlankArgumentException( "name" );
1066
1067        //---* Check for null *------------------------------------------------
1068        if( isNull( optional ) ) throw new NullArgumentException( name );
1069        final var retValue = optional.orElseThrow( () -> new EmptyArgumentException( name ) );
1070
1071        //---* Done *----------------------------------------------------------
1072        return retValue;
1073    }   //  requireNotEmptyArgument()

1684     *  @throws IllegalArgumentException {@code arg} failed the validation.
1685     *  @throws NullArgumentException   {@code arg}, {@code name},
1686     *      {@code validation} or {@code messageProvider} is {@null}.
1687     *  @throws EmptyArgumentException  {@code name} is the empty String.
1688     *
1689     *  @since 0.25.11
1690     */
1691    @API( status = STABLE, since = "0.25.11" )
1692    public static final <T> T requireValidNonNullArgument( final T arg, final String name, final Predicate<? super T> validation, final BiFunction<? super String,? super T,String> messageSupplier )
1693    {
1694        requireNotBlankArgument( name, "name" );
1695        requireNonNullArgument( messageSupplier, "messageSupplier" );
1696
1697        if( !requireNonNullArgument( validation, "validation" ).test( requireNonNullArgument( arg, "name" ) ) )
1698        {
1699            throw new IllegalArgumentException( messageSupplier.apply( name, arg ) );
1700        }
1701
1702        //---* Done *----------------------------------------------------------
1703        return arg;
1704    }   //  requireValidNonNullArgument()

1706    /**

1711     *  method.} If the value of the argument is {@null}, the text
1712     *  &quot;{@link org.tquadrat.foundation.lang.CommonConstants#NULL_STRING null}&quot;
1713     *  will be returned instead. Arrays will be converted to a String through
1714     *  calling the respective {@code toString()} method from
1715     *  {@link java.util.Arrays}
1716     *  (this distinguishes this implementation from
1717     *  {@link java.util.Objects#toString(Object,String) java.util.Objects.toString()}).
1718     *  Values of type
1719     *  {@link java.util.Date} or
1720     *  {@link java.util.Calendar}
1721     *  will be translated based on the default locale - whatever that is.
1722     *
1723     *  @param  object  The object; may be {@null}.
1724     *  @return The object's string representation.

1726     *  @see java.util.Arrays#toString(boolean[])
1727     *  @see java.util.Arrays#toString(byte[])
1728     *  @see java.util.Arrays#toString(char[])
1729     *  @see java.util.Arrays#toString(double[])
1730     *  @see java.util.Arrays#toString(float[])
1731     *  @see java.util.Arrays#toString(int[])
1732     *  @see java.util.Arrays#toString(long[])
1733     *  @see java.util.Arrays#toString(Object[])
1734     *  @see java.util.Arrays#toString(short[])
1735     *  @see java.util.Arrays#deepToString(Object[])
1736     *  @see java.util.Locale#getDefault()

1740     */

1747    /**
1748     *  <p>{@summary Converts the given argument {@code object} into a
1749     *  {@link String},
1750     *  usually by calling its
1751     *  {@link Object#toString() toString()}
1752     *  method.} If the value of the argument is {@null}, the text
1753     *  provided as the {@code nullDefault} argument will be returned
1754     *  instead.</p>
1755     *  <p>Arrays will be converted to a string through calling the respective
1756     *  {@code toString()} method from
1757     *  {@link java.util.Arrays}
1758     *  (this distinguishes this implementation from
1759     *  {@link java.util.Objects#toString(Object,String) java.util.Objects.toString(Object,String)}).</p>
1760     *  <p>Values of type
1761     *  {@link java.util.Date} or
1762     *  {@link java.util.Calendar}
1763     *  will be translated based on the
1764     *  {@link java.util.Locale#getDefault() default locale}
1765     *  – whatever that is.</p>
1766     *
1767     *  @param  object  The object; may be {@null}.
1768     *  @param  nullDefault The text that should be returned if {@code object}
1769     *      is {@null}.
1770     *  @return The object's string representation.
1771     *
1772     *  @see java.util.Arrays#toString(boolean[])
1773     *  @see java.util.Arrays#toString(byte[])
1774     *  @see java.util.Arrays#toString(char[])
1775     *  @see java.util.Arrays#toString(double[])
1776     *  @see java.util.Arrays#toString(float[])
1777     *  @see java.util.Arrays#toString(int[])
1778     *  @see java.util.Arrays#toString(long[])
1779     *  @see java.util.Arrays#toString(Object[])
1780     *  @see java.util.Arrays#toString(short[])
1781     *  @see java.util.Arrays#deepToString(Object[])
1782     *  @see java.util.Locale#getDefault()
1783     *
1784     *  @since 0.0.5
1785     */
1786    @SuppressWarnings( {"IfStatementWithTooManyBranches", "ChainOfInstanceofChecks", "OverlyComplexMethod"} )
1787    @API( status = STABLE, since = "0.0.5" )
1788    public static final String toString( final Object object, final String nullDefault )
1789    {
1790        var retValue = requireNonNullArgument( nullDefault, "nullDefault" );
1791        if( nonNull( object ) )
1792        {
1793            final var objectClass = object.getClass();
1794            if( objectClass.isArray() )
1795            {
1796                if( objectClass == byte [].class )
1797                {
1798                    retValue = Arrays.toString( (byte []) object );
1799                }
1800                else if( objectClass == short [].class )
1801                {
1802                    retValue = Arrays.toString( (short []) object );
1803                }
1804                else if( objectClass == int [].class )
1805                {
1806                    retValue = Arrays.toString( (int []) object );
1807                }
1808                else if( objectClass == long [].class )
1809                {
1810                    retValue = Arrays.toString( (long []) object );
1811                }
1812                else if( objectClass == char [].class )
1813                {
1814                    retValue = Arrays.toString( (char []) object );
1815                }
1816                else if( objectClass == float [].class )
1817                {
1818                    retValue = Arrays.toString( (float []) object );
1819                }
1820                else if( objectClass == double [].class )
1821                {
1822                    retValue = Arrays.toString( (double []) object );
1823                }
1824                else if( objectClass == boolean [].class )
1825                {
1826                    retValue = Arrays.toString( (boolean []) object );
1827                }
1828                else
1829                {
1830                    retValue = deepToString( (Object []) object );
1831                }
1832            }
1833            else
1834            {
1835                retValue = object.toString();
1836            }
1837        }
1838
1839        //---* Done *----------------------------------------------------------
1840        return retValue;
1841    }   //  toString()

1843    /**
1844     *  <p>{@summary Converts the given argument into a
1845     *  {@link String}
1846     *  using the given instance of
1847     *  {@link Stringer}.}
1848     *  If the value of the argument is {@null}, the text
1849     *  provided as the {@code nullDefault} argument will be returned
1850     *  instead.</p>

1853     *  @param  value   The object; may be {@null}.
1854     *  @param  stringer    The method that is used to convert the given object
1855     *      to a String.
1856     *  @param  nullDefault The text that should be returned if {@code object}
1857     *      is {@null}.
1858     *  @return The object's string representation.
1859     *
1860     *  @see    Stringer
1861     *
1862     *  @since 0.0.5
1863     */
1864    @API( status = STABLE, since = "0.0.5" )
1865    public static final <T> String toString( final T value, final Stringer<? super T> stringer, final String nullDefault )
1866    {
1867        requireNonNullArgument( nullDefault, "nullDefault" );
1868
1869        final var retValue = nonNull( value ) ? requireNonNullArgument( stringer, "stringer" ).toString( value ) : nullDefault;
1870
1871        //---* Done *----------------------------------------------------------
1872        return retValue;
1873    }   //  toString()
